description.narrative: (Tanzania): The Christian Social Services Commission hospital network will improve care for newborns through cost-effective mentorship programs such as peer to peer learning between facilities and the use of tele-ECHO (information communications technology that improves access to medical care that is not available consistently in remote and rural communities) on newborn resuscitation. Health facilities will be encouraged to use locally made incubators and Kangaroo Mother Care for premature babies. Regular Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) meetings will be conducted to allow staff to share their insights on how to reduce morbidity and mortality of maternal and newborns. Facilities will be supported to improve their family planning services through a well-structured referral system. Opportunities for strengthening pediatric care will also be leveraged by introducing the use of pediatric death audits in the partnering network hospitals, building on the existing MPDSR platform. Facilities not offering modern contraceptive health education and services will be linked to facilities that do offer these services. The priority target population will be postpartum mothers. Note: This activity is also receiving HIV HSS funds..
